Summary Description: Dr. JeongJin Kim is a multidisciplinary scholar at the intersection of organizational psychology, AI-human collaboration, and dynamic workplace behavior. His work advances psychometric measurement (notably attitudes toward AI at work) and applies advanced longitudinal and multilevel methods to understand how affect, attitudes, and cognitive processes unfold in real work settings. Across collaborations with US and Korean samples, Kim develops robust scales (e.g., AAAW) and employs experimental and quasi-experimental designs, experience sampling, and latent-structured modeling to illuminate how AI adoption, emotion regulation, and job dynamics shape recruitment signals, performance, and well-being. His research emphasizes translational impact—providing theoretical insights and practical guidelines for AI integration, AI-driven HR practices, and interventions to mitigate boredom and associated counterproductive behaviors. His methodological portfolio combines CFA/SEM, LCS, MLM, and EMI/ESM, underpinned by open science practices and cross-context validation.
